thesis: A 19%-ROIC, 32.5%-FCF-margin travel-IT oligopolist trades below its own 5-year minimum on every earnings multiple at a 9.38% FCF yield, where the price implies a revenue decline that its reported growth and guidance do not show.
reason: Rising quality, a 9.38% FCF yield funding buybacks, and a price below even the mechanical bear value give a favourable skew. AI/direct-booking disintermediation risk, the peer P/E premium and pending acquisitions cap conviction at 4, not 5: standard volatility-scaled core size. Holdings stay well below 15.

triggers.text: TTM ROIC falls below 12%, giving up most of the post-pandemic rise to 19.0% and signalling moat erosion rather than a cyclical dip.
TTM operating margin falls below 20%, under every year since FY2022 (21.1%), showing disintermediation is forcing price cuts.
TTM FCF margin falls below 25%, under the 31.2%-33.8% band held since FY2022, showing cash generation can no longer fund buybacks and acquisitions.
Air Distribution segment revenue in the earnings release declines year on year for two consecutive quarters, signalling structural bookings loss rather than one-off Middle East disruption.
